what: Backend query profile for the admin list endpoints (priority 4: performance)
method: Django test client on the disposable test database, one warm-up request then CaptureQueriesContext for the query count and 5 timed requests for the median latency; every row is created through the real services.
scale: 3 rows vs 60 rows, each rendered through a full ?page_size=100 page
why: A per-row query is the failure mode that turns a dashboard table into a slow page. Because the measurement renders 60 rows, an N+1 would show as roughly +57 queries.
result: 12 of 13 endpoints issue a constant number of queries as the row count grows: 0 additional queries per added row. `finance folios` is listed but rendered 0 rows (folios are created by stays, which this probe does not seed), so it is excluded from the claim rather than counted as a pass.
caveats: Local disposable test database on the development host, not production timings; only the before/after and growth relationship are meaningful, not absolute milliseconds.
Latency grows with row count through serialization and row fetch (e.g. bookings 6 → 21 ms at 60 rows). That is expected work per rendered row, not a per-row query.
Every row is created through the real services, so the seeded data is valid ERP data (permissions, approvals and ledger posting all ran).
reproduce: The profile itself was produced by a temporary one-off probe (a test that seeded 3 rows, measured, seeded 57 more, measured again, then was deleted).
The durable, shipped reproduction of the same property: cd backend && python manage.py test tests.test_query_efficiency  # Ran 17 tests ... OK
That guard class (AdminListFlatnessTests) fetches a full 100-row page twice with 20 rows added in between and requires an identical query count, and it fails if it captures zero queries.
